# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 After completing a real search for "colorbond" (type + Enter + full page load of the results page), reopening the search panel still shows "Pencarian Sebelumnya" as hidden/empty — the term was never recorded. Confirmed via direct Alpine $data inspection (recent: [] both before and after the search) and zero network requests to any recent-search endpoint (including the component's own configured deleteUrl: /steelhub/recentsearch/delete/) during the entire flow.
⚠ ErrorAfter completing a real search for "colorbond" (type + Enter + full page load of the results page), reopening the search panel still shows "Pencarian Sebelumnya" as hidden/empty — the term was never recorded. Confirmed via direct Alpine $data inspection (recent: [] both before and after the search) and zero network requests to any recent-search endpoint (including the component's own configured deleteUrl: /steelhub/recentsearch/delete/) during the entire flow.
🖼️ Live Page Screenshot — the actual front-end element click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[A] WEBSITE BUG — the "Pencarian Sebelumnya" (recent searches) feature is fully wired up on the front end (the UI section exists, and the steelhubSearch Alpine component is configured with a real deleteUrl: /steelhub/recentsearch/delete/ endpoint for removing entries) but nothing in the actual search-submission flow ever WRITES a completed search into that recent-searches store. Confirmed via direct Alpine $data inspection that the component's own recent array stays [] both before and after a real, completed search, with zero network requests fired to any recent-search-related endpoint (including the configured deleteUrl) throughout the whole flow — the save side of this feature was never implemented, only the (currently unreachable) delete side and the display markup.
❌ Problematic Code
The steelhubSearch Alpine component's search-submission handler (the
function bound to the search form's real GET submission, or an
onSubmit/Enter handler) has no call to persist the completed query —
e.g. no localStorage.setItem() call and no POST/AJAX call to a
recent-search "add" endpoint (the config only defines `deleteUrl`,
with no corresponding `addUrl`/`saveUrl` at all, suggesting the save
half of this feature was never built).
✅ Fixed Code
// Inside steelhubSearch()'s submit handler, before/alongside the real
// form submission:
submitSearch() {
    if (this.query && this.query.trim()) {
        this.recent = [this.query, ...this.recent.filter(q => q !== this.query)].slice(0, 5);
        localStorage.setItem('steelhub_recent_search', JSON.stringify(this.recent));
    }
    this.$refs.searchForm.submit(); // existing real GET submission
}

1. Confirm with the dev team whether "Pencarian Sebelumnya" was meant to persist client-side (localStorage, matching the pattern of this site's other steelhub_* localStorage keys already observed elsewhere in this engagement — recently_viewed_product, steelhub_wishlist, etc.) or server-side (a real addUrl endpoint, matching how deleteUrl already works) — the fix differs depending on the intended architecture. 2. Implement the missing "save on search" step in the submit handler, matching whichever pattern is confirmed in step 1. 3. Re-test this exact flow (search + reload + reopen panel) to confirm the term now appears under "Pencarian Sebelumnya", and that removing it via the existing deleteUrl endpoint still works afterward.

23 - [Negative] Verify a SQL-injection-looking query is safely handled — page renders normally with no server/DB error leaked
Fixed 2026-08-12 — the original assertion assumed this query always returns zero results, which broke because the catalog now contains a literal test product ("SMARTRUSS® test1", SKU/name containing "1") that coincidentally full-text-matches the query string's "1" characters — a real catalog-content coincidence, not a SQL injection, confirmed via a direct page-content check (a normal 200 response, standard PLP template, one real matching product card, no DB/SQL error text anywhere). The safety property this test actually needs to verify is "no raw server/DB error is leaked and the query is rendered as inert text," not "always zero results," which is fragile against catalog content changes.
